newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of July 14, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Computer Associates Intl is the latest company to jump on the Java train and this week it will unveil a Java front end for its Unicenter TNG enterprise management system software, and support for the Java Management application programming interface, PC Week reported July 14.

Sun Microsystems Inc will unveil a draft specification for a smart card operating system called JavaCard 2.0 at Internet World in Chicago that will provide developers with a common set of APIs to build smart cards that tie into desktop applications and Internet applications, PC Week reportd July 14.

COMPUTERWORLD - Some key hardcore Apple Computer Inc users said they are finally giving up the ghost after the troubled company last week ousted CEO Gil Amelio, just 17 months after he vowed Apple's problems were fixable, Computerworld reported July 14.

In interviews last week, a half-dozen corporate Apple users, with more than 10,000 Macintosh seats, said they are phasing out or expect to drastically reduce the numbers of Macs they are using over the next several years.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Major PC vendors have fired the first salvo against Dell Computer Corp, turning savings from more efficient manufacturing and distribution into lower prices and leading the way is Compaq Computer Corp . Hewlett-Packard Co expects to have a channel assembly program in place October 1, CRN reported July 14.

Novell Inc is making progress on the business front, but internally the company is showing signs of turmoil, with Jim Tolonen, Novell's longtime chief financial officer, about to leave the company, Novell insiders told CRN. Already Vic Langford, senior vice president of Internet strategies, has already left the company, CRN reported July 14.

INFOWORLD - Analysts say PC price will continue to fall as major computer makers cut prices and refine their distribution model in an attempt to compete with Dell Computer Co, Infoworld reported on July 14.

Customers are reporting problems with the Internet Mail Access Protocl 4, or IMAP4, support in Netscape Communications Corp Communicatior product, leading some to to believe that the product was not tested thoroughly before it was released, Infoworld reported on July 14.

INFORMATION WEEK - Companies have started outsourcing on a more specific basis to save money and retain some in-house control over their IT systems, Information Week said in its July 14 issue. IT executives are learning to play one vendor off another in the bidding process and source out services for the lowest price. DirecTV, SmithKline Beecham and Chevron are some of the companies leading the new trend.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Suppliers blame overproduction by South Korean and Japanese memory makers for weak prices, for 64-mbit DRAMs, which are falling so sharply that many insiders now question whether the industry's rapid shit to high-density parts is starting to backfire, Electronic Buyers News reported July 14.

EE TIMES - At least one expert familiar with Intel Corp's "BIOS Update" technology - which quickly fixes bugs that crop up in microprocessors - says that the technology may contain a hole that could enable hackers to vandalize computers, EE Times reported July 14.
NEC electronics this week will unveil the porting of MIcrosoft Corp's Windows CE software to its MIPS core to for non-handheld device applicaitions, EE Times said on July 14.

MACWEEK - Few members of the Mac community expressed sadness or surprise at the resignation of Apple CEO Gil Amelio last week and many developers said Amelio didn't supply the market focus Apple needed, MacWeek reported July 14.

Ellen Hancock, Apple Computer Inc's former technology chief, said in an exclusive interview with MacWeek that given the opportunity, she would serve as Apple CEO. She also stressed that Apple will need both a customer and technology-focused leader, MacWeek reported July 14.
